_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.rom:D8D5: Per-slot init (X=0..2): zeroes ScoreDigitsA/B/C/D (rom:sub_D8D5 -- CONFIRMED score storage: sub_DDA9/sub_DE1C below do SED/ADC BCD arithmetic directly into these four arrays, carrying digit-place to digit-place). Then seeds ram_2119/ram_211A/ram_211B from dat_D97D,X where X=ram_1FCB.
comments.rom:DDA9: CONFIRMED (SED at rom:DDAE, BCD arithmetic): adds the caller's A/Y-held BCD point value into ScoreDigitsA/B/C/D for slot X, doubling the add when ram_2122==3 (a bonus-multiplier state). Falls through to sub_DE1C's extra-life check on every score change -- not a separate poll.
comments.rom:DE1C: Extra-life threshold check, run after every score add (see rom:DDA9). Subtracts NextLifeThreshold{Lo,Hi},X from the score; if the score has reached it, advances the threshold by BCD $0120 and -- if ExtraLifeAwardCount,X is still under 6 and the ram_00DE,X bit-6 'no more bonuses' flag isn't set -- increments ExtraLifeAwardCount,X (the actual life award). LIVE-OBSERVED (tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp): ram_210E (slot 0, the only active slot in this 1-player recording) moves through 0/1/2 across the session rather than sitting still, consistent with real awards happening, matching the user's report of getting extra lives -- not confirmed frame-exact against a specific award moment this pass.
comments.rom:D840: The main per-frame loop (jumped back into from rom:D86E after an NMI-synced wait on ram_2108 bit7). Runs, in order: sub_E25E (coin/start-switch and attract-mode front end), sub_E4F6, sub_DA51 (sound-effect trigger checks -- see dat_C8F8), sub_DEFD, sub_DCFF, sub_EB74, sub_EE3B, sub_F1D6, sub_F476, sub_F00F, sub_E8FF. None of these are individually named by content yet except sub_DA51's role, inferred from what it calls.
comments.rom:C7FC: CONFIRMED (static init loop + LIVE, tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp): builds the centipede. Loop runs X=0 while X<ram_0044 (a generic zero-page temp, not renamed -- reused 20 places for unrelated things), writing CentipedeSegRow,X (seeded from ram_2107) and CentipedeSegCol,X (from a running total in ram_0040, advanced each iteration by a fixed step in ram_0042 -- an LCG-shaped generator, also snapshotting the running pointer into ram_005C,X, a plausible per-segment 'erratic movement' seed, not confirmed). LIVE: CentipedeSegRow ($00D0-$00DB) and CentipedeSegCol ($00E2-$00ED) are each exactly 12 bytes and both churn on nearly every one of 500 one-second snapshots across the whole recording -- matches the classic 12-segment centipede exactly. After the loop, segment 0 (the head) gets its position perturbed specially (EOR #$30 on its column, ORA #$23 on its row) -- likely placing the head at its canonical start position/orientation rather than the loop's generic placement.
comments.rom:C825: Segment-count-mismatch branch, right after the build loop above: if the number of segments just placed (the loop's final count) doesn't equal CentipedeSegTarget (rom:sub_D8D5's dat_D97D-seeded value), falls through to more setup instead of the rom:C8A0 skip. STRONG CANDIDATE for the bottom-of-screen multi-head-spawn mechanic the user specifically described watching ("centipede heads spawn" when the running centipede doesn't fill its target segment count) -- not yet confirmed against a live frame where that spawn visibly happens; the recording wasn't correlated to this exact branch this pass.
comments.rom:E728: CONFIRMED shape, not yet named: looks like new-life/new-wave setup -- clears ram_00DC/ram_00DD and ram_1FC7 bit 7, then seeds several position-pair variables (ram_006A-6D, ram_007C-7F, ram_00F0/F1) with fixed constants. Candidate for player-ship and/or flea/scorpion starting positions; not confirmed against live position data this pass.
comments.rom:ED45: VEC_ED45/sub_ED64. CONFIRMED (found via the ram_vectors scan, then hand-added since one of the two writers uses LDA/LDY+STA/STY -- the scanner only tracks LDA/STA pairs, see rom:EDA1): a two-handler DLI ping-pong chain through ram_00F4/ram_00F5, the exact same mechanism Ballblazer used. VEC_ED45 sets CTRL=$40, CHARBASE=$C1 (inside chr_rom_C2AC) then re-arms itself to sub_ED64 for the next interrupt. sub_ED64 sets CTRL=$4B, CHARBASE=$39 (a different MARIA graphics-bank value, not yet mapped to a ROM range), increments the frame counter (ram_2100), calls sub_CD16/sub_F1D6/sub_CEE5, then re-arms VEC_ED45. Two more RAM-vector writers were already known (rom:D883/rom:E2EE set it to $C298 -- the 'normal' per-frame handler; rom:EC09 sets it to $ED45, i.e. this chain) but hadn't been declared as reachable entries before this pass, so all the code below ram_ED41's real 4-byte data table had been sitting unclaimed.
comments.rom:CD16: sub_CD16/sub_CD68: the per-row MARIA zone slot allocator, and (via sub_CD68) the centipede's own renderer. sub_CD16 resets a 22-entry table of zone base pointers (ram_1825, ram_1874, ... ram_1EEA, each ~79 bytes apart, spanning the $18xx-$1Exx display-list zone pages) and a parallel 23-byte 'slots used per zone' counter array at ram_0044-ram_005A (ram_0044 is reused elsewhere as a plain zero-page temp too -- this is a second, distinct use, not a naming conflict in the ROM, just in this annotation's choice not to rename a heavily-overloaded byte). sub_CD68 reads CentipedeSegRow,X, maps it to a zone index (row>>3-ish), checks that zone's slot counter against a capacity limit (#$45), and -- CONFIRMS, from the code side, what tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua's live data already suggested -- computes a display-list address for the segment from dat_C0B0,Y/dat_C098,Y (the same per-zone base tables sub_DB6C uses) and advances the zone's slot counter. This is very likely the general-purpose object-to-zone placer, not centipede-specific, given how generic the mechanism is; only the centipede's call into it has been traced so far.

headers.rom:C000: chr_rom_C000/chr_rom_C2AC. CONFIRMED (not guessed): both writers of CHARBASE (rom:D88D, rom:EC75) load #$C0 immediately before the write, so this is the real indirect-mode character set base, not just a visual match. gfx.py's default indirect-mode render at $C000 shows a readable digit/letter set followed by recognizable game sprites. DOUBLE RETRACTION this session, both caught while tracing gameplay logic, both left visible rather than silently fixed: (1) an earlier pass extended this block's end all the way to $CEE5 on the strength of live display-list refs scattered up to $CEE4, reasoning 'one continuous sheet, no gap' -- wrong, it never checked whether anything inside was also a JSR/JMP *target*. rom:C798, rom:C8AC, rom:C8D5 and rom:C8F8 (a heavily-used sound-effect dispatcher, called from 13 places in the real game loop, e.g. sub_DA51) are all real code. (2) the immediate fix (shrinking the block to end at rom:C798) was ITSELF still wrong in a worse way: it left a `gfx:true` declaration spanning ENTRY_Irq (rom:C2AB) -- and disasm.py's forced_data check unconditionally wins over an `entries` seed (see tools/disasm.py's trace loop: `if loc in self.forced_data: break`, checked before the opcode is even read), so the declared block had been silently suppressing the IRQ handler's own disassembly the whole time, label and all -- it showed as `.byte $40` under an `ENTRY_Irq:` label instead of `RTI`. Caught by noticing the entry point rendered as data at all, which should never happen for a hardware-vector-confirmed entry. Fixed by removing the block outright and re-deriving boundaries only from what the unblocked tracer and the live evidence actually agree on: ENTRY_Irq is genuinely one byte (`RTI` -- this cartridge doesn't use POKEY's IRQ features, matching the ROM notes), sitting as an isolated one-byte code island in the middle of the character sheet. The sheet itself is now two blocks either side of it -- chr_rom_C000 ($C000-$C2AA) and chr_rom_C2AC ($C2AC-$C797, tile data through $C796, zero-padded tail, code starts cleanly at $C798) -- both with dense live display-list refs on both sides of the IRQ byte, confirming the split rather than assuming it. Lesson for this ROM specifically: a `gfx:true` block is a hard override, not a hint -- never let one span a confirmed entry point, and after declaring one, grep every `dat_<addr>` label it creates against `J(SR|MP)` in the regenerated listing before trusting the boundary. The '©1984 ATARI' copyright text and enemy sprite fragments render inside the two chr_rom blocks as an indirect-mode grid.
headers.rom:D000: GameSpritesB. CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp, same session as chr_rom_C000): a second, separate direct-mode sprite sheet, referenced from all 8 line-planar pages ($D000, $D100, ... $D700 -- the classic base+n*256 pattern for an 8-line-tall object) with real widths seen at every page, not a guess from byte patterns alone. Sits between chr_rom_C2AC and ENTRY_Nmi (already-confirmed real code at $D800) with no gap either side. Checked for the same JSR/JMP-into-the-block bug found in chr_rom_C000: none found (grep for `J(SR|MP)\s+dat_D[0-7]` across the whole listing is empty), so this block's boundary is not suspect the same way. Not yet identified by content (which enemy or effect these specific graphics belong to) -- that needs a screenshot cross-check against a chosen frame's live display list, not attempted this pass.
headers.rom:C946: The $C946-$CEE4 gap, right after chr_rom_C2AC's code interruption and right before sub_CEE5 (real code, reached via rom:E2FC). Checked the same way as the F4F2 gap below: no JSR/JMP in the whole listing targets anything inside this range, but the live display-list walk (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp) found two genuine runtime-constructed graphics references landing in it -- $C9A8 (width 21) and $CEC6 (width 31, running exactly to $CEE5 with zero padding, i.e. touching sub_CEE5 with no gap at all). Declared only those two confirmed spans as gfx blocks (gfx_C9A8, gfx_CEC6); the rest of the 1439 bytes stays an honest, unconfirmed gap on the same reasoning as $F4F2-$FFFF -- sparse live evidence inside a range is enough to call its *character* (graphics, not missed code) but not enough to claim the whole span without guessing.
headers.rom:F4F2: The $F4F2-$FFFF gap. Investigated two ways this session: (1) a PC-tagged read-tap on the whole range (tools/probe-gap-readers.lua, run-01.inp, 1,183,549 hits) -- every representative top-hit PC checked resolved to either a busy-wait loop (rom:D861 BIT ram_2108/BMI L_D861) or an address that falls inside the already-confirmed chr_rom_C000 block (impossible as a real 6502 PC) -- i.e. MARIA DMA misattribution artifacts, not real readers (see docs/pitfalls.md in the toolkit). Trial entries at rom:F900 and rom:F902 both failed to produce a sustained instruction trace. (2) tools/live-slots.lua's own display-list walk -- the same live method that confirmed chr_rom_C000 and GameSpritesB -- found three genuine runtime-constructed graphics-object references landing inside this range: $FE0C (width 31), $FE64 (width 30), $FF24 (width 17); see the gfx_FE0C/gfx_FE64/gfx_FF24 blocks. Conclusion: this is a graphics region, not unreached code -- but run-01.inp only exercised a small fraction of it (3 confirmed starts out of 2830 bytes), so most of the range stays an honest, unconfirmed gap rather than a guessed block. A recording that reaches more enemy/bonus varieties, or 2-player mode, would likely close more of it.

blocks.name: chr_rom_C000
blocks.note: Character/sprite tile data, indirect-mode. Ends exactly where ENTRY_Irq's single RTI byte begins. See the header note -- this boundary replaces two earlier, wrong versions.

blocks.name: chr_rom_C2AC
blocks.note: Continuation of the tile sheet, resuming right after ENTRY_Irq's single RTI byte. Ends at $C797 (zero-padded tail); code (sub_C798) starts cleanly at $C798. See the header note.

blocks.name: gfx_C9A8
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp), width 21. See the rom:C946 header note.

blocks.name: gfx_CEC6
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp), width 31, runs exactly up to sub_CEE5 (real code) with zero padding in between. See the rom:C946 header note.

blocks.name: GameSpritesB
blocks.note: Second sprite sheet, direct-mode, all 8 line-planar pages confirmed live. See the header note.

blocks.name: dat_D97D
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: 4-entry table indexed by ram_1FCB, read at rom:D8EA and seeded into ram_2119/ram_211A/ram_211B (CentipedeSegTarget) at rom:sub_D8D5. Already rendered correctly as data by the default fallback; declared here only to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_DBF2
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: four small tables (dat_DBF2, dat_DBF7, dat_DBFC, dat_DC01) feeding the fixed-position/fixed-graphic display-list-entry builders at sub_DBA4 and L_DBE7. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_F168
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: 4-entry table indexed by ram_1FCB (same shape as dat_D97D), read at rom:E740 and seeded into ram_1FC5. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_E225
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: 34-byte table read (indexed) at rom:E20F, feeding ram_00FC. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_EFE7
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: three small tables (dat_EFE7, dat_F007, dat_F00B) read from rom:EF91/L_EF96. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_CFDB
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: five 2-byte tables (dat_CFDB/CFDD/CFDF/CFE1/CFE3) read from several places in the CF00-CFE5 code, running exactly up to sub_CFE5 (real code) with no gap. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_F1CC
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: two 5-byte tables (dat_F1CC, dat_F1D1) read from rom:F255 and rom:D855, running exactly up to sub_F1D6 (real code) with no gap. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: dat_ED20
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: four small tables (dat_ED20, dat_ED2C, dat_ED32, dat_ED41 -- the last one genuinely only 4 bytes, see rom:ED45's header note for the retraction of an earlier, wrong reading that treated the real code starting right after it as part of the same table) running exactly up to VEC_ED45 (real code) with no gap. Already rendered correctly as data; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap.

blocks.name: gfx_FE0C
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp): a display list built at runtime referenced this exact ROM address as a direct-mode object graphic, width 31 (the widest a single MARIA object entry can encode). Raw bytes at this address also happen to contain a byte pair that decodes as a plausible-looking JMP into already-confirmed code -- a coincidence, not evidence of code: any 2-byte value in $C000-$FFFF has decent odds of looking like a valid JMP target in a ROM this densely populated with real code, and the live DL reference is the stronger, dynamic evidence. Not yet identified by content. See the $F4F2-$FFFF gap note below.

blocks.name: gfx_FE64
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE, same run and same caveat as gfx_FE0C (width 30). Not yet identified by content.

blocks.name: gfx_FF24
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE, same run and same caveat as gfx_FE0C (width 17). Not yet identified by content.

blocks.name: InterruptVectors
blocks.note: The standard 6502 NMI/RESET/IRQ vector table. Bytes read back as $D800/$D804/$C2AB, which match ENTRY_Nmi/ENTRY_Reset/ENTRY_Irq exactly -- confirmed by agreement, not guessed.
